reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G2-NA-Q4-Harden (mat_g2_na_q4_3), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The generator directly fulfills both core learning actions outlined in the competency: representing and identifying similar fractions with denominators up to 8. Visual identification is practiced through items asking "What fraction does the model show?" (seeds 42, 43, 45, 46, 502), while active representation is directly tested via tasks such as "Shade 3/8 of the shape." (seed 44) and "Shade 4/5 of the shape." (seed 500).

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample demonstrates broad coverage across the target denominator set {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8} specified by the MATATAG curriculum. The items evaluate fractions with fourths ("Shade 2/4 of the shape."), fifths ("What fraction does the model show?"), sixths ("What fraction does the model show?"), and eighths ("Shade 7/8 of the shape."), encompassing both unit and non-unit proper fractions.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive demand is fully appropriate for Grade 2 Quarter 4 learners. Prompts like "What fraction does the model show?" and "Shade 3/8 of the shape." use clear, minimal language that focuses on visual-spatial fraction recognition and partition shading without introducing unnecessary textual complexity or multi-step arithmetic.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The samples utilize multiple complementary formatters, including multiple-choice recognition (`read_mcq`) in "What fraction does the model show?" and interactive construction (`set_click`) in "Shade 4/5 of the shape." and "Shade 7/8 of the shape.". Distractors effectively probe standard misconceptions such as reciprocal/inverted fractions (e.g., 5/2, 4/3, 8/1, 6/5) and complementary unshaded parts (e.g., 3/5, 1/4, 7/8, 1/6).

competency_alignment.rationale: All generated items align strictly with the target competency text. Items such as "What fraction does the model show?" and "Shade 2/4 of the shape." evaluate fraction concept identification and representation without introducing out-of-scope concepts like fraction addition, subtraction, or decimals.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical values and fraction dimensions strictly adhere to the Grade 2 scale bounds. Denominators and numerators remain within single digits (denominators 4, 5, 6, 8) and all fractions are proper (less than or equal to 1), as seen in "Shade 3/8 of the shape." and "What fraction does the model show?".
